notes: METHOD AND LIMITS: The WebSearch budget ran out after about 5 calls, and WebFetch is blocked for genome.ch.bbc.co.uk, bbc.co.uk, bbc.com, news.bbc.co.uk, theguardian.com, nytimes.com, telegraph.co.uk, independent.co.uk, reuters.com and apnews.com. So almost everything was verified by opening Wikipedia pages (series pages, List of Wildlife on One episodes, List of Natural World episodes, BBC Wildlife Specials, honours lists, award pages) that state exact dates and cite BBC Genome/Radio Times. I could not follow those citations to the BBC pages themselves. NEWS CELLS (kind news): the article URLs are the ones Wikipedia cites for Attenborough, but I could not open them; the month comes from the date printed in the Wikipedia citation (and, for Guardian URLs, from the date in the URL). Marked confirmed true on that basis; treat them as slightly weaker than the series/honours cells. EPISODE CELLS: Wildlife on One (1977-2005), BBC Wildlife Specials (narrated by him to 2008) and Natural World (only episodes whose Presenter/narrator cell names him) are real dated broadcast listings, one episode chosen per month. They add coverage but are low-profile; trim them first if the grid feels padded. Months with a bigger event show that event instead. HONOURS: the London Gazette pages are scanned images I could not read, so the CBE (7 Jun 1974), knighthood (15 Jun 1985), CVO (14 Jun 1991) and CH (list published 29-30 Dec 1995, so placed at 1995-12 although it is the 1996 New Year Honours) months come from the Wikipedia honours lists, which cite those Gazette issues. OM date (10 Jun 2005) is from the Wikipedia Order of Merit members list. GCMG is from the Birthday Honours list published 10 Oct 2020 (delayed by COVID). CONFLICTS RESOLVED: Planet Earth Peabody - main text says April 2008, a reference says May 2008; used 2008-05 (ceremony). Trials of Life first aired 3 Oct 1990 and The Living Planet 19 Jan 1984 per the Wikipedia series pages (not 17 Oct / 18 Jan). The Tribal Eye aired 27 May 1975 (book 1976), not 1976. STILL TO CONFIRM (13 cells, month is a placeholder, year known): Director of programmes 1969, Cherry Kearton Medal 1972, leaving BBC management (early 1973 per Wikipedia), Eastwards with Attenborough (Oct 1973 comes only from listing-site snippets, not an authoritative source), BAFTA Fellowship 1980, Kalinga Prize 1981, FRS 1983 (Royal Society page gives year only; month is a guess), Kew Medal 1996, Jane Oriel dies (early 1997 per The Life of Birds page), Cosmos Prize 2000, Faraday Prize 2003, Descartes Prize 2004, Prince of Asturias 2009 (ceremony is each October; no announcement date found). THIN AREAS: 1967-1978 is the weakest (BBC Genome blocked): 1968, 1970, 1976 and 1986 have no cell; 1990 has one; the 1980s and 1990s have almost no news items because the news archives were blocked. Only 1969-07 (Pot Black), 1969-02 (Civilisation), 1967-07/12, 1971-12, 1972-12, 1973-12 and 1974-06 were found for the Controller/Director years. FROM MEMORY: nothing was added from memory; every cell traces to a page I opened, except the three-line existing placeholders listed above. Existing 1985-01 Knighted, 2024-01 Stephen Hawking Medal and 2009-01 Prince of Asturias were moved (see removed). Sub-claims worth a second look: 2008-05 "enters the political jungle" Telegraph headline was dropped in favour of the Peabody cell; 2013-09 cell uses the Guardian URL slug (human evolution stopped) because the Wikipedia citation title did not match the slug. EXCEEDS TARGET: 259 confirmed of 719 months (36.0 percent), above the 20-30 percent aim, mainly because of the episode-listing cells.
